messages.content: Return strict JSON only. Act as a hostile ICLR reviewer of this proposed world-model security claim. Score novelty 0-10 and decide ACCEPT_SCREEN or REJECT. Distinguish ordinary support/OOD shift, offline RL causal confusion, and actual security mechanism. The project has already rejected generic rollout compounding, replay bias, uncertainty manipulation, reward inversion, action aliasing, rank coupling, temporal dither, optimizer state, and non-normal transient amplification. A screen must be runnable in native MBRL-Lib or official TD-MPC2 and preserve legal simulator transitions. Give exact conditions that would make it genuinely distinct and a short gate if accepted.

{"candidate": "Broad claim: Under a shared learned world model, an attacker can use only legally generated trajectories whose action marginal and single-step factual loss remain matched to benign exploration, yet state-dependent action assignment creates a causal-confounding blind spot: the model predicts observed policy trajectories accurately but learns the wrong interventional action effect, so native counterfactual MPC selects systematically harmful actions. The operation is a deterministic feedback controller that assigns a pre-sampled action multiset to states by pole-angle/velocity rank, preserving the action histogram and all ground-truth transitions; controls are independent random assignment, equal action marginals, and an intervention-coverage audit. Evaluate one-step on held-out behavior data and on counterfactual action swaps, then native CEM return.", "priors": ["Causal World Models by Unsupervised Deconfounding of Physical Dynamics (arXiv:2012.14228)", "Can Active Sampling Reduce Causal Confusion in Offline RL?
